sub: Named after the woman who pleaded (tujādiluka) in ayah 1
theme: Allah hears everything, from one wife’s quiet complaint to secret plotting. So keep His limits, whisper only about good, show manners in gatherings, and give your deepest loyalty to Allah.
story: Revealed in Madinah, probably after the Battle of the Trench. Aws ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit, an elderly man, told his wife Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah in anger, “You are to me like my mother’s back.” Before Islam, this ẓihār ended a marriage forever.

She came to the Prophet ﷺ, who had no ruling yet. She kept pleading: her youth was spent, her children were small, and she raised her complaint to Allah. ʿĀʾishah, in the same room, missed some of her words. Allah heard all of it.

The rest of the surah guides Madinah through other problems: secret whispering against the believers, manners in the Prophet’s ﷺ gatherings, and the hypocrites. It ends by drawing the line between Satan’s party and Allah’s party.

sections.title: Allah hears Khawlah’s plea; ẓihār doesn’t end marriage but needs expiation
sections.meaning: Allah heard Khawlah’s plea. Ẓihār, likening your wife to your mother, is false and ugly, and it doesn’t end a marriage. A husband who says it must make amends before returning to his wife. Those who defy Allah’s limits will be humbled, and every forgotten deed is counted.
points: Allah heard the woman pleading about her husband
Wives are not mothers; ẓihār is an ugly lie
Free a slave, else fast two months, else feed sixty
Defiers are humbled; Allah counted what they forgot
sections.matters: It shows Allah’s care: one woman’s complaint in the corner of a room became a ruling for everyone. It ends a harsh custom from before Islam and sets Allah’s limits above old habits in family life.
sections.story: Khawlah’s elderly husband declared ẓihār on her in anger. The Prophet ﷺ had no revelation about it yet and said she seemed unlawful to him. She kept pleading for herself and her young children, and complained to Allah, until these ayat came.
explained: Before Islam, ẓihār ended a marriage forever, worse than divorce. Khawlah had given her husband her youth and her wealth. Her children were small: left with him they would be neglected, kept with her they would go hungry. So she argued her case and turned to Allah. The answer: saying it doesn’t turn a wife into a mother.

It is still a sinful, false thing to say. Before being intimate again, the husband frees a slave; if he can’t, he fasts two months in a row; if he can’t, he feeds sixty poor people. These are Allah’s limits. Whoever defies them is humbled, and on that Day Allah reminds them of every deed.
teaches: Allah hears every complaint, even one whispered in a corner.
Take your problems to Allah, and keep asking.
A false word about your spouse carries a real cost.
You forget your deeds; Allah keeps count.
sections.hook: The name comes from tujādiluka in ayah 1. The expiation steps down in order: free a slave → fast two months → feed sixty. “Before they touch one another” appears in both 3 and 4.

sections.title: Allah knows every secret whisper; some plot, but believers talk only good
sections.meaning: Allah knows all in the heavens and earth: no three whisper without Him as the fourth. Some kept plotting in secret and twisted their greeting to the Prophet ﷺ. Believers may talk privately, but only about good. Whispering that frightens believers comes from Shayṭān, and can’t harm them without Allah’s permission.
points: Three whisper, He is the fourth; five, He is the sixth
They returned to secret plotting and a twisted greeting
Believers: talk privately about good and taqwā, never sin
Harmful whispering is from Shayṭān; rely on Allah
sections.matters: Secret plotting feels safe because no one else knows. This section removes that illusion: Allah is present in every private talk. It also protects the community, since whispers that make others anxious are Shayṭān’s tool, and the believer’s answer is trust in Allah.
sections.story: Reportedly some Jews of Madinah, who had a peace treaty with the Muslims, and some hypocrites whispered whenever a believer passed, making him fear a plot or bad news. Told to stop, they carried on. Some greeted the Prophet ﷺ with “as-sāmu ʿalayka,” death be upon you.
explained: Private talk feels hidden, but Allah is with every group by His knowledge, however small or large, and on the Day of Resurrection He tells them what they said. Some had been told to stop whispering against the believers, yet went back to it, plotting sin, aggression and defiance of the Prophet ﷺ.

They even said “death be upon you” in place of salām, then reasoned: if he were a prophet, we’d be punished. The Prophet ﷺ answered only, “And upon you.” Hell is enough for them. Believers may whisper too, but about righteousness and taqwā. Frightening whispers come from Shayṭān and can’t hurt without Allah’s permission.
teaches: No talk is truly secret: Allah is always the fourth.
Keep private conversations for good things.
Don’t whisper with one person while leaving a third out.
Answer insults without becoming rude yourself.
A delayed punishment is not a cancelled one.
sections.hook: Najwā runs through all four ayat, 7 to 10. Ayah 7 counts up: three → fourth, five → sixth. The trio “sin, aggression, disobedience to the Messenger” appears in 8 and again in 9.

sections.title: Make room in gatherings; charity before consulting the Prophet ﷺ, later lifted
sections.meaning: Two lessons in manners. In gatherings, make room for others and get up when asked; Allah raises believers and people of knowledge. Before a private talk with the Prophet ﷺ, give charity first. When that proved hard, Allah lifted it and kept the core duties: prayer, zakah and obedience.
points: Make room, Allah makes room; rise, Allah raises you
Give charity before a private talk with the Prophet ﷺ
Rule lifted; keep up prayer, zakah and obedience
sections.matters: Good manners are part of faith. Making room or standing up can feel like losing your place, but Allah says it raises you. The charity rule protected the Prophet’s ﷺ time, and its quick removal shows how gently Allah eases a burden.
sections.story: Reportedly Badr veterans arrived at a crowded gathering and found no room, so the Prophet ﷺ asked some others to stand, and they disliked it. Ayah 12 came when endless private questions burdened him. Reportedly only ʿAlī acted on it before ayah 13 lifted it.
explained: People held on to seats near the Prophet ﷺ and wouldn’t shift for newcomers. Allah says: make room, and He will make room for you. When told to get up, whether to leave, to pray or to do any good, get up. It doesn’t lower you: Allah raises believers, and those given knowledge, by degrees.

Some kept the Prophet ﷺ in long private talks, crowding out others. So Allah required a charity first, excusing those who had nothing. Many then stopped coming even for real needs. Allah pardoned them and lifted the rule, reportedly after an hour or ten nights, leaving prayer, zakah and obedience in its place.
teaches: Make space for others; Allah will make space for you.
Humility and knowledge raise a person, not a seat.
Respect the time of teachers and leaders.
Allah eases a rule when it becomes too hard.
sections.hook: Ayat 11 and 12 open “O you who have believed.” In 11 the reward echoes the act: make room → Allah makes room. Ayat 11 and 13 end “Allah is Aware of what you do.”

sections.title: Hypocrites with false oaths are Satan’s party; loyal believers are Allah’s party
sections.meaning: Hypocrites befriend those Allah is angry with, belong to neither side, and hide behind false oaths. Wealth won’t save them, and they will swear falsely even to Allah. Satan has taken them over. Allah and His messengers will prevail. True believers put loyalty to Allah above family: they are Allah’s party.
points: Hypocrites side with Allah’s enemies, hiding behind false oaths
Nothing saves them; they lie even to Allah; Satan’s party loses
Defiers humiliated; Allah and His messengers will prevail
No love for Allah’s enemies, even family: Allah’s party succeeds
sections.matters: The surah closes with the test of sincere faith. Swearing and appearances are not enough. Where your deepest loyalty lies shows which party you belong to, and only one of the two parties wins.
sections.story: Reportedly about ʿAbdullāh ibn Nabtal, a hypocrite who passed on the Prophet’s ﷺ talk to others, then swore he hadn’t insulted him and brought friends who swore too. Ayah 22 is reportedly about Companions who faced their own relatives in battle, such as Abū ʿUbaydah.
explained: The hypocrites sided secretly with the believers’ enemies while claiming Islam, belonging to neither side. Their oaths were a junnah, a shield: people believed them and were turned from Allah’s way. Wealth and children won’t save them. On that Day they’ll swear to Allah too, still thinking it works. Shayṭān has made them forget Allah.

Those who defy Allah end up humiliated, because Allah has written that He and His messengers will prevail. Real believers don’t give heartfelt love and loyalty to those at war with Allah and His Messenger, even close family. This is not about ordinary kindness or fair dealing. Allah writes faith in their hearts and is pleased with them.
teaches: False oaths may fool people, never Allah.
Forgetting Allah’s remembrance is how Shayṭān takes over.
Truth wins in the end, by proof and by Allah’s help.
Put loyalty to Allah above every other tie.
Allah’s pleasure is the real success.
sections.hook: Two matching lines: “the party of Satan, they are the losers” (19) and “the party of Allah, they are the successful” (22). The family list in 22 runs fathers → sons → brothers → kindred.

groups.text: Allah heard Khawlah pleading about her husband and complaining to Him.
Ẓihār doesn’t make a wife a mother; it is a false, ugly statement.
To return to his wife, he frees a slave, or fasts two months, or feeds sixty poor people.
Those who defy Allah are humbled; on that Day He recounts every forgotten deed.
No group whispers without Allah being with them in knowledge.
Some kept plotting in secret and greeted the Prophet ﷺ with a curse.
Believers talk privately only about good; harmful whispering is Shayṭān’s, so rely on Allah.
Make room in gatherings and rise when asked; Allah raises believers and the learned.
Charity before a private talk with the Prophet ﷺ, then lifted: keep prayer, zakah and obedience.
Hypocrites befriend Allah’s enemies and hide behind false oaths.
Nothing saves them; they’ll swear even to Allah. They are Satan’s losing party.
Defiers are humiliated; Allah has decreed that He and His messengers will prevail.
Believers put Allah before family; Allah is pleased with them. They are His successful party.

1.explain: Tujādiluka: she argued her case with you, again and again. Khawlah pleaded about her husband and complained to Allah. ʿĀʾishah, in the same room, missed some words. Allah, as-Samīʿ al-Baṣīr, heard them all.
1.why: Aws ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit, old and short-tempered, declared ẓihār on his wife Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah. The Prophet ﷺ had no ruling yet. She kept pleading, “He used up my youth… O Allah, I complain to You,” until Jibrīl brought this ayah.

2.explain: Ẓihār: a husband saying, “You are to me like my mother’s back.” It doesn’t make her his mother. It is munkar and zūr, an ugly, false statement. Still, Allah pardons and forgives.

3.explain: If he wants to go back on his words, either to be intimate again or simply to keep her as his wife, he must first free a slave. This ruling is a warning to deter it.

4.explain: If he can’t, he fasts two consecutive months before intimacy; if he can’t fast, he feeds sixty poor people. These are ḥudūd Allāh, limits not to cross. Acting on them is part of true faith.
4.why: Reportedly, when these ayat came, Khawlah said her husband had no slave, was too old to fast, and couldn’t feed sixty people. The Prophet ﷺ gave a basket of dates, she added another, and it was given in charity for him.

5.explain: Yuḥāddūn: those who defy Allah and His Messenger. Kubitū: they will be humbled, like earlier nations who defied their messengers. Clear signs have come, so there is no excuse, and a humiliating punishment awaits.

6.explain: On that Day Allah raises everyone and tells them what they did. Aḥṣāhu Allāhu wa nasūh: He kept count of every deed while they forgot it. Nothing escapes Him.

7.explain: Najwā: a private, whispered talk. With any three, Allah is the fourth; with any five, He is the sixth. He is with them by His knowledge, hearing and seeing, wherever they are.
7.why: Reportedly about a group who did something in secret: either hypocrites or some Jews of Madinah. Allah let them know that nothing is hidden from Him.

8.explain: Those told to stop whispering went back to it, plotting ithm (sin), ʿudwān (aggression) and defiance of the Prophet ﷺ. Twisting the greeting, they said “death be upon you,” then asked why Allah didn’t punish them. Hell is enough.
8.why: Reportedly some Jews of Madinah, under a peace treaty, whispered whenever a believer passed, so he feared a plot. Told to stop, they carried on. Some greeted the Prophet ﷺ with “as-sāmu ʿalayka”; he simply replied, “And upon you.”

9.explain: Believers may talk privately, but never about sin, aggression or disobeying the Prophet ﷺ. Talk instead about al-birr, every kind of good, and taqwā. Remember you will be gathered before Allah.
9.why: Reportedly the hypocrites kept holding secret meetings that worried the believers, and this ayah and the next were revealed.

10.explain: Harmful whispering comes from Shayṭān, to make believers anxious. It can’t hurt them at all unless Allah permits, so rely on Him. Two people shouldn’t whisper apart from a third, as it upsets him.

11.explain: Tafassaḥū: make room when you sit together, and Allah makes room for you. Unshuzū: when told to get up, get up, to leave, pray or do good. Humbling yourself this way raises you by degrees.
11.why: Reportedly some Badr veterans arrived at a crowded gathering and stood waiting, but no one made room. The Prophet ﷺ asked some others to stand for them. Those moved disliked it, and hypocrites criticised it.

12.explain: Before a private talk with the Prophet ﷺ, give ṣadaqah first. It is better for you and purer. Anyone who can’t afford it is excused: Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
12.why: People kept asking the Prophet ﷺ so many private questions that it became hard on him, or the wealthy took up his time from the poor. Reportedly only ʿAlī acted on it, giving a dinar first.

13.explain: Did you fear giving charity first? Since you didn’t, and Allah pardoned you, the rule was lifted, reportedly after an hour or ten nights. What remains: prayer, zakah and obeying Allah and His Messenger.
13.why: Many stopped consulting the Prophet ﷺ even for real needs. ʿAlī reportedly told him people couldn’t afford a dinar and suggested a barley grain’s weight of gold. Then this ayah came, and ʿAlī said, “Through me Allah lightened it.”

14.explain: Have you seen the hypocrites who befriend a people Allah is angry with? They belong to neither side. They swear falsely that they are believers, knowing they are lying.
14.why: Reportedly about ʿAbdullāh ibn Nabtal, a hypocrite who sat with the Prophet ﷺ and carried his words to the Jews. Asked why he insulted him, he swore he hadn’t, then brought friends who swore the same.

15.explain: Allah has prepared a severe punishment for them. What they did was truly evil: helping the believers’ enemies and deceiving the believers.

16.explain: They used their oaths as a junnah, a shield hiding their disbelief and protecting their lives and wealth. Fooled by those oaths, people were turned from Allah’s way. Their punishment is humiliating.

17.explain: Neither their wealth nor their children will help them against Allah at all. They are the people of the Fire, there forever.

18.explain: On the Day of Resurrection they will swear to Allah just as they swore to you, thinking it will help. Whoever lives on a path dies on it. They are the liars.
18.why: The same report continues: after the hypocrite and his friends swore falsely, Allah revealed this passage, down to “the losers” in ayah 19.

19.explain: Istaḥwadha: Shayṭān took them over and made them forget remembering Allah. They are ḥizb ash-shayṭān, Satan’s party, the losers of this life and the next.

20.explain: Those who defy Allah and His Messenger will be among al-adhallīn, the most humiliated, in this life and the next.

21.explain: Allah has decreed: “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.” They prevail by proof, and when ordered to fight, in battle too. Allah is Strong and Mighty, so His promise cannot fail.
21.why: Reportedly believers hoped that after Makkah, Ṭāʾif and Khaybar, Allah would open Persia and Rome to them. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy scoffed that those empires were far stronger, and this ayah came.

22.explain: Believers don’t give love and loyalty to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even fathers, sons, brothers or kindred. Allah has written faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a rūḥ from Him: His strength, light or help.
22.why: Reportedly about Companions who faced their own relatives in battle when those relatives fought Islam, such as Abū ʿUbaydah and Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr. Another report links it to Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah.
